author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: A generalized ordinal association model for twoway contingency tables is obtained by using the BoxCox family of power transformations to scale the interaction between row and column classifications Goodmans RC model and the rank correlation model which are the most commonly used ordinal association models are special cases of the proposed generalized model Several properties of the new model are derived which lead to meaningful interpretations of the model and the association parameter The present results also unify the similar results known for the RC model and the rank correlation model

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: This study investigates the treatment variances observed in repeated measures bioavailability trials which are crucial for evaluating the efficacy and safety of pharmaceutical formulations Utilizing a diverse dataset comprised of multiple bioavailability studies we applied a mixedeffects model to assess the variability associated with different treatment groups over time Our analysis emphasizes the role of intra and intersubject variability as well as the influence of baseline characteristics on treatment outcomes We employed advanced statistical techniques including ANOVA and nested variance components analysis to compare the treatment variances providing a comprehensive understanding of the sources of variability Our findings reveal significant differences in treatment variances among various formulations highlighting the importance of considering these variances when designing bioavailability studies and interpreting their results These insights pave the way for improved methodologies in drug efficacy assessment and inform regulatory decisionmaking processes in the pharmaceutical industry The results underscore the necessity of careful consideration of treatment variance in the development and approval of new therapeutics

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: The monotonicity of the critical values is essential for the implementation of a stepup multiple test procedure For a stepup test controlling the family wise error rate exactly at a while a theoretical justification of the existence of monotone critical values is available in the literature for the case of iid test statistics it is still an open problem for the general exchangeable case Recently Finner and Roters Ann Statist gave an example of three exchangeable random variables casting doubt about this existence in general We provide a positive result in this paper by proving that the critical values of a stepup test involving an equicorrelated trivariate standard normal distribution is indeed monotone when the common correlation is positive and at most zalpha zzalpha z where zalpha is the upper alpha percent point of N Our example raises the hope of establishing the desired monotonicity property in the case of test statistics with totally positive multivariate distributions in the sense of Karlin and Rinott C Elsevier Science BV

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: The concept of false discovery rate FDR which is the expected proportion of false positives type I errors among rejected hypotheses has received increasing attention recently by researchers in multiple hypotheses testing A similar measure involving false negatives type errors which we call the false negatives rate FNR is considered and an explicit formula of it is developed for a generalized stepupstepdown procedure in terms of probability distributions of ordered test statistics It is shown that a stepdown procedure can be used to control the FNR under certain conditions on the test statistics Various FDRcontrolling procedures that exist in a given multiple testing situation are further studied in terms of the FNR In particular an unbiasedness property is defined for an FDRcontrolling multiple testing procedure by the inequality FDR FNR less than or equal to The FDRcontrolling generalized stepupstepdown procedure considered in Sarkar Ann Statist in particular the Benjamini and Hochberg J Roy Statist Soc Ser B stepup procedure is proved to be unbiased when the test statistics are independent and is conjectured to be so based on simulations when they are dependent Also conjectured is the unbiasedness of the FDRcontrolling Benjamini and Lui J Statist Plarm Inference stepdown procedure with independent as well as dependent test statistics Different FDRcontrolling procedures are investigated based on simulated data from equicorrelated multivariate normals in terms of the quantity FNR FDR that reflects the strength of unbiasedness C Elsevier BV

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: Starting with a decision theoretic formulation of simultaneous testing of null hypotheses against twosided alternatives a procedure controlling the Bayesian directional false discovery rate BDFDR is developed through controlling the posterior directional false discovery rate PDFDR This is an alternative to Lewis and Thayer with a better control of the BDFDR Moreover it is optimum in the sense of being the nonrandomized part of the procedure maximizing the posterior expectation of the directional percomparison power rate given the data while controlling the PDFDR A corresponding empirical Bayes method is proposed in the context of oneway random effects model Simulation study shows that the proposed Bayes and empirical Bayes methods perform much better from a Bayesian perspective than the procedures available in the literature C Elsevier BV All fights

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: Results on the false discovery rate FDR and the false nondiscovery rate FNR are developed for singlestep multiple testing procedures In addition to verifying desirable properties of FDR and FNR as measures of error rates these results extend previously known results providing further insights particularly under dependence into the notions of FDR and FNR and related measures First considering fixed configurations of true and false null hypotheses inequalities are obtained to explain how an FDR or FNRcontrolling singlestep procedure such as a Bonferroni or Sidak procedure can potentially be improved Two families of procedures are then constructed one that modifies the FDRcontrolling and the other that modifies the FNRcontrolling Sidak procedure These are proved to control FDR or FNR under independence less conservatively than the corresponding families that modify the FDR or FNRcontrolling Bonferroni procedure Results of numerical investigations of the performance of the modified Sidak FDR procedure over its competitors are presented Second considering a mixture model where different configurations of true and false null hypotheses are assumed to have certain probabilities results are also derived that extend some of Storeys work to the dependence case

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In this paper we investigate the application of the likelihood ratio test LRT for assessing the homogeneity of variances within a covariance matrix characterized by block compound symmetry Block compound symmetry is a structure commonly encountered in multivariate data where observations exhibit correlations and variances that are uniform across defined groups or blocks We propose a rigorous statistical framework for deriving the likelihood ratio test statistic under the null hypothesis of homogeneity of variances Through simulation studies we evaluate the tests performance including its power and type I error rate under various sample sizes and covariance structures Our results demonstrate that the LRT maintains desirable statistical properties and offers a robust tool for variance homogeneity testing in block compound symmetric contexts We also provide guidance on practical implementation and interpretability of results enhancing the applicability of our findings in fields such as biostatistics social sciences and experimental research where such covariance structures frequently arise

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In this paper we introduce a novel generalized model for the analysis of associations in ordinal contingency tables a common structure used in various fields such as social sciences healthcare and market research to investigate relationships between ordinal variables Traditional methods for analyzing such data often rely on assumptions that can lead to biased results or misinterpretations Our proposed model accounts for the inherent ordinal nature of the data while incorporating a flexible framework that allows for the examination of both marginal and conditional associations We utilize advanced statistical techniques including generalized estimating equations and ordinal regression approaches to derive parameter estimates and assess the strength of associations Through extensive simulation studies we demonstrate the robustness and efficacy of our model compared to existing methods Additionally we apply our model to realworld datasets to illustrate its practical implications and advantages The findings reveal that our generalized model offers a more nuanced understanding of associations in ordinal contingency tables paving the way for more accurate and insightful data analysis in diverse research contexts

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In this paper we explore the performance of modified Simes critical values in the context of statistical testing under positive dependence among hypotheses The original Simes method which provides a powerful testing framework for multiple hypotheses traditionally assumes independence among the tests However many practical scenarios involve positive dependence which can significantly affect the validity of the method We propose new critical values tailored for this dependency structure enhancing the robustness of Simes approach Through a theoretical analysis we derive asymptotic distributions for the modified critical values establishing their consistency and effectiveness in controlling the familywise error rate under positive dependence Additionally we conduct a series of simulations to illustrate the gains in power and error control relative to both the original Simes method and other existing procedures Our findings provide valuable insights for researchers in fields such as genomics finance and social sciences where positive dependence is prevalent and underscore the need for adaptive testing methods that account for underlying correlations in hypothesis tests

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In the realm of multiple hypothesis testing controlling the False Discovery Rate FDR has emerged as a critical concern particularly in highdimensional data analysis This paper investigates the performance of stepwise procedures designed to control FDR when conducting simultaneous tests Specifically we develop a theoretical framework to assess the efficacy of various stepwise approaches in maintaining FDR at desired levels while also evaluating their impact on false negative rates FNR a lesserexplored but crucial aspect of hypothesis testing Through extensive simulations and analytical results we unveil the tradeoffs between stringent FDR control and the propensity for false negatives Our findings demonstrate that while certain stepwise procedures can achieve optimal FDR control they may inadvertently inflate FNR leading to a substantial loss of statistical power Additionally we explore modifications to existing algorithms that can enhance performance by balancing FDR and FNR This work provides valuable insights into the implications of stepwise testing strategies guiding researchers in their quest for robust inference in complex data settings

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In this paper we investigate the monotonicity properties of critical values associated with a stepup multiple testing procedure Stepup tests are widely employed in the context of controlling the false discovery rate in multiple hypothesis testing and understanding the behavior of critical values in relation to the underlying pvalues is crucial for their effective application We analyze the relationship between the ranking of pvalues and the corresponding critical values generated by a stepup procedure Using theoretical derivations and simulations we demonstrate that under certain regularity conditions the critical values exhibit a monotonic relationship as a function of the ordered pvalues This monotonicity not only provides insights into the structure of the stepup test but also aids in the development of robust methodologies for hypothesis testing Our findings have implications for practitioners in statistical analysis ensuring that the application of stepup tests adheres to stringent criteria for interpretability and reliability Ultimately this note contributes to the understanding of stepup testing frameworks and emphasizes the necessity for further exploration of their theoretical underpinnings

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In the realm of highdimensional data analysis accurately identifying significant effects while controlling for false discoveries is paramount This paper introduces a robust framework for controlling the Bayes Directional False Discovery Rate DFDR within the context of random effects models We first establish the theoretical underpinnings of DFDR in a Bayesian setting emphasizing the need for directional hypotheses in heterogeneous data Utilizing a hierarchical modeling approach we derive a methodology that combines Bayesian shrinkage techniques with empirical Bayes estimation to calibrate the DFDR effectively Through extensive simulation studies we demonstrate the efficacy of our approach in managing Type I and Type II errors while maintaining power Furthermore we apply our method to realworld datasets in genomics and neuroimaging showcasing substantial improvement in the identification of true signals in the presence of random effects Our results indicate that controlling the Bayes DFDR not only enhances interpretability but also provides a crucial tool for reliable inference in highdimensional settings This work opens new avenues for research in Bayesian statistics and its applications across various scientific fields

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In the realm of multiple hypothesis testing controlling error rates such as the Familywise Error Rate FWER and the False Discovery Rate FDR is critical for ensuring the validity of statistical inferences This paper introduces novel stepup procedures designed to control both generalized FWER and generalized FDR extending traditional frameworks to accommodate dependent testing scenarios We derive theoretical properties that demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed methods in maintaining rigorous control over these error rates while allowing for a wide range of dependence structures between hypotheses Through comprehensive simulations and realdata applications we illustrate the improved power of our stepup procedures compared to existing approaches Furthermore we discuss the implications of our findings in the broader context of statistical science and provide guidelines for practitioners aiming to implement these techniques in their analyses Our results pave the way for more reliable inferential procedures in complex decisionmaking environments thereby enhancing the robustness of conclusions drawn from multiple testing frameworks

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: A multivariate extension of Cohens J Amer Statist Assoc result on interval estimation of normal variance is made in this article Based on independent random matrices X p m and S p p distributed respectively as Npm Im and Wpn with unknown and n p the problem of obtaining confidence interval for is considered The shortest length invariant confidence interval is obtained and is shown to be improved by some other interval estimators Some new properties of the noncentral and central distributions of sample generalized variance have been proved for this purpose

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: For the problem of testing the homogeneity of the variances in a covariance matrix with a block compound symmetric structure the likelihood ratio test is derived in this paper A modification of the test that allows its distribution to be better approximated by the chisquare distribution is also considered Formulae for calculating approximate sample size and power are derived Small sample performances of these tests in the case of two dependent bivariate or trivariate normals are compared to each other and to the competing tests by simulating levels of significance and powers and recommendation is made of the ones that have good performance The recommended tests are then demonstrated in an illustrative example

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In many applications of multiple hypothesis testing where more than one false rejection can be tolerated procedures controlling error rates measuring at least k false rejections instead of at least one for some fixed k can potentially increase the ability of a procedure to detect false null hypotheses The kFWER a generalized version of the usual familywise error rate FWER is such an error rate that has recently been introduced in the literature and procedures controlling it have been proposed A further generalization of a result on the kFWER is provided in this article In addition an alternative and less conservative notion of error rate the kFDR is introduced in the same spirit as the kFWER by generalizing the usual false discovery rate FDR A kFWER procedure is constructed given any set of increasing constants by utilizing the kth order joint null distributions of the pvalues without assuming any specific form of dependence among all the pvalues Procedures controlling the kFDR are also developed by using the kth order joint null distributions of the pvalues first assuming that the sets of null and nonnull pvalues are mutually independent or they are jointly positively dependent in the sense of being multivariate totally positive of order two MTP and then discarding that assumption about the overall dependence among the pvalues

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: A modification of the critical values of Simes test is suggested in this article when the underlying test statistics are multivariate normal with a common nonnegative correlation yielding a more powerful test than the original Simes test A stepup multiple testing procedure with these modified critical values which is shown to control false discovery rate FDR is presented as a modification of the traditional BenjaminiHochberg BH procedure Simulations were carried out to compare this modified BH procedure with the BH and other modified BH procedures in terms of false nondiscovery rate FNR FDRFNR and average power The present modified BH procedure is observed to perform well compared to others when the test statistics are highly correlated and most of the hypotheses are true c Elsevier BV

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In repeated measures bioavailabilitybioequivalence studies involving two formulations the underlying measurements such as the area under the plasma concentrationtime curve AUC and the maximum plasma concentration Cmax typically have a block compoundsymmetric covariance matrix To test the equality of the variances in such a covariance matrix we derive in this paper an exact test and four asymptotic tests We compare these tests using simulation to determine those that have good performance in terms of controlling the type I error rate as well as providing good power We provide an example to demonstrate the proposed method Copyright C John Wiley Sons Ltd

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In statistical inference the construction of confidence intervals is pivotal for reliable estimation of population parameters This paper addresses the challenge of deriving shorter confidence intervals for the generalized variance a crucial metric for multivariate data analysis We propose a novel methodology that leverages advanced statistical techniques to enhance the precision and accuracy of confidence intervals associated with the generalized variance By employing a combination of the likelihoodbased approach and bootstrap resampling methods we formulate a new confidence interval that significantly reduces the interval length while maintaining the desired coverage probability Through extensive simulation studies we demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed method compared to existing techniques highlighting improvements in both bias and length of the confidence intervals Additionally we provide a theoretical underpinning for our approach ensuring robustness across various distributions and sample sizes Our findings contribute to the field of multivariate statistics by offering a practical tool for researchers and practitioners seeking more efficient inference methods for generalized variance estimation

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In the landscape of multiple hypothesis testing the management of false discoveries and nondiscoveries is crucial for maintaining the integrity of statistical inference This paper systematically investigates the interplay between False Discovery Rates FDR and False Nondiscovery Rates FNR within singlestep multiple testing procedures We introduce a framework that unifies these two concepts allowing for a nuanced understanding of how singlestep procedures can impact both type I and type II errors By conducting extensive simulations and theoretical derivations we characterize the tradeoffs between FDR and FNR under various testing paradigms including the BenjaminiHochberg procedure and its derivatives We reveal that minimizing FDR can inadvertently inflate FNR especially in settings with sparse signals or highdimensional data Our findings highlight the necessity of balancing discovery rates for effective hypothesis testing and we propose practical guidelines for researchers to optimize their procedures The implications of our results extend to fields such as genomics psychology and economics where accurate decisionmaking from multiple tests is imperative This work opens avenues for future research on multifaceted control of error rates in statistical methodologies

text: We prove that the power function of the likelihood ratio test for MANOVA attains its minimum when the rank of the location parameter matrix Theta decreases from s to This provides a theoretical justification of a result that is known in the literature based only on numerical studies C Elsevier Science

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: This paper investigates the power function of the likelihood ratio test LRT in the context of multivariate analysis of variance MANOVA The LRT is a widely adopted statistical method for testing hypotheses involving multiple dependent variables However its power can be influenced by various factors including sample size effect size and the correlation structure among the dependent variables We derive the asymptotic properties of the power function for the LRT under the MANOVA framework emphasizing the impact of these factors on the tests efficacy Simulation studies complement our theoretical findings illustrating the scenarios where the likelihood ratio test demonstrates robustness and those where it may underperform The results provide valuable insights for researchers in selecting appropriate methodologies for multivariate hypotheses testing highlighting the importance of understanding power dynamics in practical applications Our findings contribute to the existing literature by offering a comprehensive analysis of the LRTs performance in MANOVA settings and serving as a guideline for future research in multivariate statistics

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: The original definitions of false discovery rate FDR and false nondiscovery rate FNR can be understood as the frequentist risks of false rejections and false nonrejections respectively conditional on the unknown parameter while the Bayesian posterior FDR and posterior FNR are conditioned on the data From a Bayesian point of view it seems natural to take into account the uncertainties in both the parameter and the data In this spirit we propose averaging out the frequentist risks of false rejections and false nonrejections with respect to some prior distribution of the parameters to obtain the average FDR AFDR and average FNR AFNR respectively A linear combination of the AFDR and AFNR called the average Bayes error rate ABER is considered as an overall risk Some useful formulas for the AFDR AFNR and ABER are developed for normal samples with hierarchical mixture priors The idea of finding threshold values by minimizing the ABER or controlling the AFDR is illustrated using a gene expression data set Simulation studies show that the proposed approaches are more powerful and robust than the widely used FDR method Copyright c John Wiley Sons Ltd

text: Procedures controlling error rates measuring at least k false rejections instead of at least one are often desired while testing a large number of hypotheses The kFWER probability of at least k false rejections is such an error rate that has been introduced and procedures controlling it have been proposed Recently Sarkar introduced an alternative less conservative notion of error rate the kFDR generalizing the usual notion of false discovery rate FDR and proposed a procedure controlling it based on the kdimensional joint distributions of the null pvalues and assuming MTP multivariate totally positive of order two positive dependence among all the pvalues In this article we assume a less restrictive form of positive dependence than MTP and develop alternative procedures based only on the bivariate distributions of the null pvalues

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In this paper we investigate the estimation of the common mean of several normal populations using the Pitman closeness criterion a robust and meaningful approach to evaluating parameter estimation We provide a comprehensive analysis of the properties of estimators derived under this criterion including their unbiasedness consistency and efficiency Employing a Bayesian framework we derive a class of estimators and examine their performance in terms of Pitman closeness to the true common mean Through a simulation study we benchmark these estimators against traditional methods such as the sample mean and weighted averages considering various configurations of population variances and sample sizes Our results indicate that the estimators based on the Pitman closeness criterion consistently outperform classical approaches particularly in the presence of heterogeneity among population variances The implications of our findings are discussed in the context of practical applications in fields such as psychology and biomedical research where accurate estimation of common means from multiple groups is essential Our work provides a valuable contribution to the statistical literature by highlighting the advantages of utilizing the Pitman closeness criterion in the context of multiple normal populations

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In the realm of highdimensional hypothesis testing controlling the false discovery rate FDR is a critical concern particularly in the presence of dependent test statistics This paper introduces novel procedures for controlling the KFDR ktrue discoveries false discovery rate using bivariate distributions of null pvalues We begin by establishing a theoretical framework that employs the joint distribution of correlated pvalues allowing for a more accurate estimation of rates of true and false discoveries Our proposed methodologies involve a series of adjustments and thresholds derived from empirical bivariate pvalue distributions which help maintain the KFDR at a specified level while accommodating the inherent dependencies among tests Through extensive simulation studies we demonstrate that our approaches outperform existing methods in various dependency structures including positive and negative correlations We also provide an application of our procedures to real genomic data showcasing their practical utility in identifying significant associations without inflating the risk of erroneous conclusions Overall our findings underscore the importance of incorporating the correlation structure of pvalues to enhance the reliability of statistical inference in highdimensional settings

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In the field of statistics the estimation of a common mean across multiple multivariate normal populations presents both theoretical challenges and practical implications This paper investigates the shrinkage properties of several conventional estimators employed in this context including the sample mean the pooled estimator and the JamesStein estimator We utilize a comparative framework to explore the shrinkage domination of these estimators providing rigorous mathematical proofs and simulations that illustrate their performance under various parameter settings Our findings reveal that under certain conditions shrinkage estimators can outperform traditional methods in terms of mean squared error MSE especially as the number of populations increases Additionally we examine the implications of our results for practical applications highlighting scenarios where the adoption of shrinkage techniques can lead to substantial improvements in estimation accuracy This work contributes to the ongoing discourse on optimal estimation strategies in multivariate settings offering insights that may influence both theoretical research and applied statistical practices

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In statistical inference the construction of confidence intervals for the generalized variance a pivotal measure in multivariate analysis is essential for understanding the underlying data structure Traditional methods often yield intervals that can be overly conservative leading to inefficient estimation of variance parameters This paper presents novel Steintype improvements to confidence intervals for the generalized variance building upon the foundational work of Stein on shrinkage estimators By incorporating Steins principles into the construction of confidence intervals we derive more accurate and efficient estimators that utilize information from the data more effectively We develop theoretical results demonstrating the improved coverage properties and reduced expected lengths of the proposed intervals compared to conventional approaches Through Monte Carlo simulations and realdata applications we illustrate the practical advantages of our methodology highlighting its robustness across various sample sizes and configurations These findings offer significant contributions to multivariate statistical methodologies and enhance the reliability of variance assessments in complex data scenarios

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In bioinformatics the identification of differentially expressed genes DEGs from microarray experiments is crucial for understanding underlying biological processes Traditional statistical approaches often fall short in accurately determining significance thresholds leading to either false positives or missed discoveries This paper presents a Bayesian framework for establishing thresholds that enhance the reliability of DEG identification We propose a model that incorporates prior distributions reflecting biological knowledge and experimental variability allowing for the adjustment of thresholds based on empirical data We utilize a hierarchical Bayesian approach that accounts for multiple testing and the dependence between genes resulting in a more nuanced consideration of expression patterns Through simulations and real microarray datasets we demonstrate that our Bayesian method outperforms conventional approaches by balancing sensitivity and specificity offering a more robust mechanism for DEG detection Our findings underscore the potential of Bayesian techniques in refining statistical thresholds for genomics ultimately fostering more accurate insights into gene expression dynamics in various biological contexts

author: Sanat K. Sarkar

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: AbstractThis paper presents a comprehensive decisiontheoretic framework for controlling the false discovery rate FDR and false nondiscovery rate FNR from a Bayesian perspective Traditional methods for managing these rates often rely on frequentist approaches which may not adequately address the underlying uncertainty inherent in statistical decisions We propose a unified Bayesian model that integrates prior beliefs and posterior probabilities to formulate optimal decision rules By employing a loss function that accounts for the tradeoffs between FDR and FNR we derive procedures that minimize expected loss under varying decision thresholds Our approach not only enhances the interpretability of FDR and FNR control but also allows for the incorporation of prior information leading to more informed decisions in hypothesis testing contexts We provide theoretical results demonstrating the efficacy of our methods and illustrate their practical application through simulations and realworld case studies The findings underscore the utility of a Bayesian perspective in balancing the risks associated with false discoveries and missed identifications offering a robust alternative to traditional statistical methodologies Keywords false discovery rate false nondiscovery rate Bayesian statistics decision theory hypothesis testing

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: A general decision theoretic formulation is given to multiple testing allowing descriptions of measures of false discoveries and false nondiscoveries in terms of certain loss functions even when randomized decisions are made on the hypotheses Randomized as well as nonrandomized procedures controlling the Bayes false discovery rate BFDR and Bayes false nondiscovery rate BFNR are developed These are applicable in any situation unlike the corresponding frequentist procedures that control the BFDR or BFNR but do so under certain dependence structures of the test statistics Even in the presence of such dependence as simulations show the proposed procedures perform much better than the corresponding frequentist procedures They provide better control of the BFDR or BFNR than those for which control is achieved through local FDR or local FNR

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: Selective inference using multiple confidence intervals is an emerging area of statistical research whose importance is being realized very recently We consider making such inference in the context of analyzing data with sparse signals in a Bayesian framework Although the traditional posterior credible intervals are immune to selection they can have low power in detecting the true signals because of covering nosignal too often if the sparse nature of the data is not properly taken into account We demonstrate this phenomenon using a canonical Bayes model with the parameters of interest following a zeroinflated mixture prior We propose a new method of constructing multiple intervals for any given selection rule taking a Bayesian decision theoretic approach under such a model It involves the local fdr the posterior probability of a parameter being null which is commonly used in multiple testing It controls an overall measure of error rate the Bayes or posterior false coverage rate at a desired level among the selected intervals We apply this method to the regression problem and demonstrate via simulations as well as data analyses that it is much more powerful in terms of enclosing zero less frequently than the traditional and some alternative methods

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: Some new probability inequalities involving the ordered components of an MTP random vector are derived which provide an analytical proof of an important conjecture in the field of multiple hypothesis testing This conjecture has been mostly validated so far using simulation

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: The Simes method for testing intersection of more than two hypotheses is known to control the probability of type I error only when the underlying test statistics are independent Although this method is more powerful than the classical Bonferroni method it is not known whether it is conservative when the test statistics are dependent This article proves that for multivariate distributions exhibiting a type of positive dependence that arise in many multiplehypothesis testing situations the Simes method indeed controls the probability of type I error This extends some results established very recently in the special case of two hypotheses

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: This paper explores the properties of ordered random variables exhibiting the multivariate total positivity of order two MTP structure focusing on the derivation and application of key probability inequalities We establish several fundamental inequalities that extend the current understanding of MTP random variables and their ordered characteristics Our main contribution is a comprehensive proof of the Simes conjecture which posits a specific relationship among the ordered MTP random variables in the context of multiple comparisons By leveraging the inherent properties of MTP distributions we provide a rigorous mathematical framework that not only validates the conjecture but also offers new insights into the behavior of ordered probability measures Additionally we discuss the implications of our findings on statistical inference and their potential applications in various fields including econometrics and bioinformatics where ordered dependencies are prevalent Through this work we aim to enrich the interdisciplinary dialogue surrounding probability inequalities and their foundational role in statistical theory

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: The false discovery rate FDR is a crucial measure in the context of multiple hypothesis testing particularly in highdimensional data settings where many null hypotheses are tested simultaneously This paper investigates the behavior of FDR in various stepwise multiple testing procedures which have gained prominence due to their balance between Type I error control and power enhancement We first establish theoretical results regarding the FDR under common stepwise approaches such as the Holm and BenjaminiHochberg procedures under different dependency structures among hypotheses Through extensive simulations we explore the practical implications of our theoretical findings highlighting the conditions under which stepwise procedures either preserve or exacerbate FDR rates Additionally we propose modified versions of existing methods aimed at improving FDR control without a significant loss in statistical power Our results demonstrate that while stepwise procedures can offer flexibility and robustness careful consideration of their assumptions and contexts is essential to maintain reliable FDR levels We conclude with recommendations for practitioners in choosing appropriate testing strategies based on the underlying data characteristics and research objectives

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: The probability of false discovery proportion FDP exceeding gamma is an element of controlling the gammaFDP under similar positive dependence condition assumed in that paper We offer better alternatives of the stepdown and stepup procedures in Romano and Shaikh using pairwise joint distributions of the null pvalues We generalize the notion of gammaFDP making it appropriate in situations where one is willing to tolerate a few false rejections or due to high dependency some false rejections are inevitable and provide methods that control this generalized gammaFDP in two different scenarios i only the marginal pvalues are available and ii the marginal pvalues as well as the common pairwise joint distributions of the null pvalues are available and assuming both positive dependence and arbitrary dependence conditions on the pvalues in each scenario Our theoretical findings are being supported through numerical studies

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In this paper we investigate the covariances associated with order statistics derived from dependent random variables While much of the existing literature has focused on independent random variables our work addresses the complexities introduced by dependence which is often encountered in practical applications We derive new expressions for the covariances between order statistics and their associated random variables highlighting the impact of various dependence structures on these relationships Our results extend the classical theory of order statistics by providing formulas that incorporate copulabased dependence measures We also present illustrative examples to demonstrate the applicability of our findings across different scenarios including both continuous and discrete distributions Finally we discuss potential implications for statistical inference and estimation especially in fields where dependent variables are common such as finance and environmental science These new insights contribute to a deeper understanding of how dependence influences the behavior of order statistics and offer tools for further research in the field of statistical dependence

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: The concept of false discovery rate FDR has been receiving increasing attention by researchers in multiple hypotheses testing This paper produces some theoretical results on the FDR in the context of stepwise multiple testing procedures with dependent test statistics It was recently shown by Benjamini and Yekutieli that the BenjaminiHochberg stepup procedure controls the FDR when the test statistics are positively dependent in a certain sense This paper strengthens their work by showing that the critical values of that procedure can be used in a much more general stepwise procedure under similar positive dependency It is also shown that the FDRcontrolling BenjaminiLiu stepdown procedure originally developed for independent test statistics works even when the test statistics are positively dependent in some sense An explicit expression for the FDR of a generalized stepwise procedure and an upper bound to the FDR of a stepdown procedure are obtained in terms of probability distributions of ordered components of dependent random variables before establishing the main results

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In the realm of statistical hypothesis testing controlling the False Discovery Proportion FDP has gained considerable attention due to its relevance in highdimensional data settings such as genomics and brain imaging This paper presents further results on methodologies designed to maintain stringent control over the FDP when conducting multiple comparisons Building on existing frameworks we propose enhanced techniques that incorporate adaptive thresholding and simulationbased calibration approaches demonstrating their effectiveness in various data scenarios We derive theoretical bounds for the FDP under these methods and provide empirical evidence through extensive simulations and realdata applications Our findings indicate that the proposed strategies not only preserve the desired level of confidence but also improve power thus offering a more reliable approach for researchers aiming to identify true positive findings in largescale studies These results contribute to the ongoing discourse on optimal methods for false discovery control paving the way for future research aimed at balancing discovery and reliability in inferential statistics

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In the realm of multiple hypothesis testing controlling the familywise error rate FWER is crucial for maintaining the reliability of scientific conclusions The Simes method a wellestablished procedure has been traditionally applied under the assumption of independence among test statistics However many practical scenarios involve positively dependent test statistics which can lead to suboptimal performance of standard multiple testing procedures In this paper we extend the Simes method to accommodate positively dependent test statistics by leveraging the concepts of dependence structure and correlation inequalities We conduct a thorough theoretical analysis to establish the validity and efficacy of the modified Simes procedure demonstrating that it maintains control over the FWER while improving power in settings characterized by positive dependence Through a series of Monte Carlo simulations and real data applications we illustrate the advantages of our approach compared to traditional methods Our findings highlight the importance of appropriately accounting for dependency structures in multiple hypothesis testing frameworks and provide a robust alternative for researchers dealing with positively dependent data The proposed methodology is straightforward to implement and contributes to the growing recognition of the complexities involved in modern statistical inference

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In the frequency analysis of several time series observed simultaneously it is often necessary to adapt classical results of linear models and multiple regression to situations involving complexvalued variates Given a realvalued stochastic time series Yt and a suitable vectorvalued fixed series Xt with components Xi t j r t it may be of interest to assess the effect in the frequency domain of each component series of Xt on the behavior of Yt If values of Yt and Xt are made available for t T then under certain conditions and for large T at frequency the finite Fourier transform of Yt is approximately linearly related to the finite Fourier transform of Xt through a complexvalued vector A In an asymptotic sense A with entries Aj j r may be interpreted as a vector of complex regression coefficients of Yt on Xt at frequency The amount of amplification and phase shift by which the Xi t series must be modified in order to give an optimum fit on average to the Yt series at frequency is therefore determined by the realvalued gain Gj Aj and phase j arg Aj respectively of Yt over Xj t After estimating Aj and also Gj and j using results from multiple regression analysis adapted to complexvalued variates a gain plot and a phase plot can be made for each j r with appropriate confidence regions drawn on the plot at each frequency to assess the degree of association between Yt and the Xj t series In this article new asymptotic simultaneous confidence regions for gains and phases are derived and we show theoretically that they are shorter than similar confidence regions currently available in the statistical literature The tools used here for constructing these improved regions include a differential identity for the complex multivariate Gaussian distribution and a multivariate probability inequality for the amplitudes of components of a complexvalued Gaussian random vector Numerical computations covering a variety of possible situations show the actual amount of asymptotic improvement Empirical investigations of the finite sample behavior of the proposed new simultaneous confidence regions indicate good overall performance

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: Abstract Based on independent samples from several multivariate normal populations possibly of different dimensions the problem of simultaneous estimation of the mean vectors is considered assuming that the covariance matrices are unknown Two loss functions the sum of usual quadratic losses and the sum of arbitrary quadratic losses are used A class of minimax estimators generalizing the JamesStein estimator is obtained It is shown that these estimators improve the usual set of sample mean vectors uniformly under the sum of quadratic losses This result is extended to the sum of arbitrary quadratic losses under some restrictions on the covariance matrices

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: AbstractIn this paper we address the problem of simultaneous estimation of independent normalmean vectors when the covariance matrices are unknown Estimating mean vectors accurately is crucial in various statistical applications yet traditional methods often fall short when the covariance structure is not fully specified We propose a novel estimation framework that integrates both empirical Bayes and frequentist approaches to derive a robust estimator for the mean vectors leveraging information from the independent samples while accounting for the uncertainty in the covariance matrices Our method utilizes the structure of the normal distribution to provide a consistent estimator of the mean vectors alongside a strategy for estimating the covariance matrices based on observed data We establish the asymptotic properties of the proposed estimator demonstrating its consistency and efficiency under mild conditions Through simulation studies and realworld data applications we illustrate the practical performance of our method compared to existing techniques highlighting significant improvements in bias and mean squared error Our findings contribute to the statistical methodology for multivariate analysis of independent normal vectors with implications for fields such as biomedical research and quality control

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: AbstractIn this paper we introduce a novel methodology for conducting simultaneous confidence region analyses in the context of frequency analysis of multiple timeseries data Unraveling the intricate relationships among several timeseries variables often requires an understanding of their frequencydomain characteristics Traditional approaches typically evaluate each timeseries individually potentially overlooking the dependence structures among them Our proposed method utilizes a multivariate spectral approach incorporating techniques from both spectral estimation and simultaneous inference We derive a set of confidence regions that account for the correlations between multiple timeseries ensuring accurate interpretation across various frequencies Through both theoretical derivations and simulation studies we demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in maintaining control over the overall Type I error rate even in the presence of highdimensional data Application to realworld datasets manifests the practical significance of our method highlighting its capacity to elucidate underlying patterns and interdependencies in multivariate timeseries analyses This work not only advances the statistical framework for frequency analysis but also provides practitioners with a robust tool for exploring complex temporal dynamics in a simultaneous context

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: A general decision theoretic formulation is given to multiple testing allowing descriptions of measures of false discoveries and false nondiscoveries in terms of certain loss functions even when randomized decisions are made on the hypotheses Randomized as well as nonrandomized procedures controlling the Bayes false discovery rate BFDR and Bayes false nondiscovery rate BFNR are developed These are applicable in any situation unlike the corresponding frequentist procedures that control the BFDR or BFNR but do so under certain dependence structures of the test statistics Even in the presence of such dependence as simulations show the proposed procedures perform much better than the corresponding frequentist procedures They provide better control of the BFDR or BFNR than those for which control is achieved through local FDR or local FNR

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: For the problem of estimating the common mean of k normal populations the performance of the GraybillDeal estimator is compared with each of the k sample means using the criterion of Pitman closeness It is shown that for the GraybillDeal estimator to dominate any of the sample means it is necessary and sufficient that Ni the size of the sample from population i is greaterthanorequalto for all i when k and it is sufficient that Ni SIGMAj notequal iNj Ni greaterthanorequalto for all i when k where Ni minj notequal iNj This is a generalization of the result obtained by Kubokawa

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: Formulas for covariance matrix between a random vector and its ordered components are derived for different distributions including multivariate normal t and F The present formulas and related results obtained here lead to some known results in the literature as special cases C Academic Press Inc

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In many scientific fields particularly in emerging technologies and highthroughput experiments analysts often encounter sparse signals which can obscure the true parameter estimates and their associated uncertainties Traditional methods for constructing confidence intervals may struggle in these scenarios due to limited data and noise This paper presents a Bayesian approach to constructing multiple confidence intervals for selected parameters that enhances robustness and interpretability in the presence of sparse signals By leveraging prior distributions and Bayesian updating our method allows for the incorporation of existing knowledge which can significantly improve estimation accuracy and interval coverage We employ hierarchical modeling techniques to account for the dependencies among parameters and provide formal guidelines for prior selection based on the characteristics of the underlying signal Through simulation studies and realdata applications we demonstrate the advantages of our Bayesian framework in producing credible intervals that outperform classical methods in terms of coverage probability and precision in sparse settings This research establishes a new avenue for extracting meaningful insights from limited datasets facilitating more reliable inference in various applications including genomics finance and environmental monitoring

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: AbstractThis paper presents a comprehensive decisiontheoretic framework for controlling the false discovery rate FDR and false nondiscovery rate FNR from a Bayesian perspective Traditional methods for managing these rates often rely on frequentist approaches which may not adequately address the underlying uncertainty inherent in statistical decisions We propose a unified Bayesian model that integrates prior beliefs and posterior probabilities to formulate optimal decision rules By employing a loss function that accounts for the tradeoffs between FDR and FNR we derive procedures that minimize expected loss under varying decision thresholds Our approach not only enhances the interpretability of FDR and FNR control but also allows for the incorporation of prior information leading to more informed decisions in hypothesis testing contexts We provide theoretical results demonstrating the efficacy of our methods and illustrate their practical application through simulations and realworld case studies The findings underscore the utility of a Bayesian perspective in balancing the risks associated with false discoveries and missed identifications offering a robust alternative to traditional statistical methodologies Keywords false discovery rate false nondiscovery rate Bayesian statistics decision theory hypothesis testing

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: Procedures controlling error rates measuring at least k false rejections instead of at least one are often desired while testing a large number of hypotheses The kFWER probability of at least k false rejections is such an error rate that has been introduced and procedures controlling it have been proposed Recently Sarkar introduced an alternative less conservative notion of error rate the kFDR generalizing the usual notion of false discovery rate FDR and proposed a procedure controlling it based on the kdimensional joint distributions of the null pvalues and assuming MTP multivariate totally positive of order two positive dependence among all the pvalues In this article we assume a less restrictive form of positive dependence than MTP and develop alternative procedures based only on the bivariate distributions of the null pvalues

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: This paper explores the relationship between the multivariatet distribution and the Simes inequality a critical tool in multihypothesis testing We begin by providing a comprehensive review of the properties of the multivariatet distribution highlighting its relevance in modeling correlated data particularly in small sample sizes and scenarios with heavytailed distributions We then introduce the Simes inequality and its role in managing Type I error rates in multiple comparison procedures Our analysis presents conditions under which the Simes inequality can be applied to test hypotheses derived from multivariatet distributed variables Through a series of simulations we demonstrate the effectiveness of the Simes inequality in controlling familywise error rates when applied to multivariatet data Furthermore we provide theoretical proofs to establish the robustness of the Simes inequality in this context The findings of this paper contribute to the literature by extending the application of the Simes inequality offering a valuable approach for researchers dealing with multivariate data in various fields including finance biology and social sciences

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: This paper explores the properties of ordered random variables exhibiting the multivariate total positivity of order two MTP structure focusing on the derivation and application of key probability inequalities We establish several fundamental inequalities that extend the current understanding of MTP random variables and their ordered characteristics Our main contribution is a comprehensive proof of the Simes conjecture which posits a specific relationship among the ordered MTP random variables in the context of multiple comparisons By leveraging the inherent properties of MTP distributions we provide a rigorous mathematical framework that not only validates the conjecture but also offers new insights into the behavior of ordered probability measures Additionally we discuss the implications of our findings on statistical inference and their potential applications in various fields including econometrics and bioinformatics where ordered dependencies are prevalent Through this work we aim to enrich the interdisciplinary dialogue surrounding probability inequalities and their foundational role in statistical theory

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: The study of vegetation fluctuations gives valuable information toward effective land use and development We consider this problem for the East African region based on the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index NDVI series from satellite remote sensing data collected between and over kilometer grid points We detect areas with significant increasing or decreasing monotonic vegetation changes using a multiple testing procedure controlling the mixed directional false discovery rate mdFDR Specifically we use a threestage directional BenjaminiHochberg BH procedure with proven mdFDR control under independence and a suitable adaptive version of it The performance of these procedures is studied through simulations before applying them to the vegetation data Our analysis shows increasing vegetation in the Northern hemisphere as well as coastal Tanzania and generally decreasing Southern hemisphere vegetation trends which are consistent with historical evidence

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: The severity of type II errors is frequently ignored when deriving a multiple testing procedure even though utilizing it properly can greatly help in making correct decisions This paper puts forward a theory behind developing a multiple testing procedure that can incorporate the type II error severity and is optimal in the sense of minimizing a measure of false nondiscoveries among all procedures controlling a measure of false discoveries The theory is developed under a general model allowing arbitrary dependence by taking a compound decision theoretic approach to multiple testing with a loss function incorporating the type II error severity We present this optimal procedure in its oracle form and offer numerical evidence of its superior performance over relevant competitors C Elsevier Inc

text: Some new probability inequalities involving the ordered components of an MTP random vector are derived which provide an analytical proof of an important conjecture in the field of multiple hypothesis testing This conjecture has been mostly validated so far using simulation

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: Sarkar showed that certain positively dependent MTP random variables satisfy the Simes inequality The multivariatet distribution does not satisfy this MTP property so other means are necessary A corollary was given in Sarkar to handle this distribution but there is an error In this paper a direct proof is given to show the multivariatet does satisfy the Simes inequality C Published by Elsevier BV
