text: The false discovery rate FDR is a crucial measure in the context of multiple hypothesis testing particularly in highdimensional data settings where many null hypotheses are tested simultaneously This paper investigates the behavior of FDR in various stepwise multiple testing procedures which have gained prominence due to their balance between Type I error control and power enhancement We first establish theoretical results regarding the FDR under common stepwise approaches such as the Holm and BenjaminiHochberg procedures under different dependency structures among hypotheses Through extensive simulations we explore the practical implications of our theoretical findings highlighting the conditions under which stepwise procedures either preserve or exacerbate FDR rates Additionally we propose modified versions of existing methods aimed at improving FDR control without a significant loss in statistical power Our results demonstrate that while stepwise procedures can offer flexibility and robustness careful consideration of their assumptions and contexts is essential to maintain reliable FDR levels We conclude with recommendations for practitioners in choosing appropriate testing strategies based on the underlying data characteristics and research objectives

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In this paper we introduce a novel generalized model for the analysis of associations in ordinal contingency tables a common structure used in various fields such as social sciences healthcare and market research to investigate relationships between ordinal variables Traditional methods for analyzing such data often rely on assumptions that can lead to biased results or misinterpretations Our proposed model accounts for the inherent ordinal nature of the data while incorporating a flexible framework that allows for the examination of both marginal and conditional associations We utilize advanced statistical techniques including generalized estimating equations and ordinal regression approaches to derive parameter estimates and assess the strength of associations Through extensive simulation studies we demonstrate the robustness and efficacy of our model compared to existing methods Additionally we apply our model to realworld datasets to illustrate its practical implications and advantages The findings reveal that our generalized model offers a more nuanced understanding of associations in ordinal contingency tables paving the way for more accurate and insightful data analysis in diverse research contexts

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In this paper we present a comprehensive extension of Simes test and Hochbergs stepup procedure two foundational methods for addressing multiple hypothesis testing in statistical analysis While both methods are widely employed their applications often face constraints due to underlying assumptions and limited adaptability to complex experimental designs Our proposed generalization introduces novel techniques that enhance robustness in scenarios with dependent pvalues and allows for a broader range of error control beyond the traditional familywise error rate FWER Through extensive simulations we demonstrate that our methods maintain desirable power properties while achieving improved Type I error rates across diverse settings We also provide a theoretical foundation for our generalization by deriving new asymptotic results that align existing paradigms with practical implementations Our findings suggest that the generalization of Simes test and Hochbergs procedure significantly augments their utility in contemporary statistical practice facilitating more reliable inferences in the face of multiple comparisons in a variety of research fields

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: AbstractIn the realm of statistical inference deriving valid confidence intervals is crucial for effective decisionmaking This paper introduces invariant confidence sequences for key parameters in a multivariate linear regression model addressing the limitations of traditional approaches that often assume homogeneity across coefficients We leverage the properties of the multivariate normal distribution to construct sequential confidence intervals that maintain their validity across diverse parameter configurations and data structures Our method employs a generalization of the classical Fishers method and incorporates the principles of invariance under linear transformations ensuring robust performance regardless of the covariance structure Through a series of simulations and realdata applications we illustrate the practical advantages of our proposed confidence sequences over traditional methods in terms of coverage probability and interval length The findings highlight the flexibility and efficiency of invariant confidence sequences paving the way for further advancements in multivariate regression analysis We conclude by discussing potential extensions of our methodology to other statistical models and its implications for future research in the field

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: For the problem of testing the homogeneity of the covariance matrices of several dependent multivariate normals a likelihood ratio test is derived in this paper The software SAS can be used to perform the test and the code is given and explained Several modifications of the test that allow their distributions to be better approximated by the chisquare distribution are also considered Formulae for calculating approximate sample size and power are derived Small sample performances of these tests in the case of two dependent bivariate normals are compared to each other and to the competing tests by simulating levels of significance and powers and recommendation is made of the ones that have good performance The recommended tests are then applied to real data from a crossover bioequivalence trial C Elsevier Science BV

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In a multiple testing problem where one is willing to tolerate a few false rejections procedure controlling the familywise error rate FWER can potentially be improved in terms of its ability to detect false null hypotheses by generalizing it to control the kFWER the probability of falsely rejecting at least k null hypotheses for some fixed k Simes test for testing the intersection null hypothesis is generalized to control the kFWER weakly that is under the intersection null hypothesis and Hochbergs stepup procedure for simultaneous testing of the individual null hypotheses is generalized to control the kFWER strongly that is under any configuration of the true and false null hypotheses The proposed generalizations are developed utilizing joint null distributions of the kdimensional subsets of the pvalues assumed to be identical The generalized Simes test is proved to control the kFWER weakly under the multivariate totally positive of order two MTP condition V Multivariate Analysis of the joint null distribution of the Pvalues by generalizing the original Simes inequality It is more powerful to detect k or more false null hypotheses than the original Simes test when the pvalues are independent A stepdown procedure strongly controlling the kFWER a version of generalized Holms procedure that is different from and more powerful than with independent pvalues is derived before proposing the generalized Hochbergs procedure The strong control of the kFWER for the generalized Hochbergs procedure is established in situations where the generalized Simes test is known to control its kFWER weakly

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: A generalized ordinal association model for twoway contingency tables is obtained by using the BoxCox family of power transformations to scale the interaction between row and column classifications Goodmans RC model and the rank correlation model which are the most commonly used ordinal association models are special cases of the proposed generalized model Several properties of the new model are derived which lead to meaningful interpretations of the model and the association parameter The present results also unify the similar results known for the RC model and the rank correlation model

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In multivariate statistical analysis assessing the homogeneity of covariance matrices is crucial for understanding the relationships among variables when dealing with dependent multivariate normal data This paper introduces a likelihood ratio test LRT specifically designed to evaluate the homogeneity of covariance matrices across different groups of dependent multivariate normal observations We derive the test statistic under the null hypothesis of equal covariance matrices and demonstrate its asymptotic properties Furthermore we propose several modifications to the standard LRT to enhance its robustness and performance in finite samples including adjustments for small sample sizes and considerations for potential violations of normality and independence Through extensive simulation studies we compare the performance of our proposed tests with traditional methods highlighting their efficacy in various statistical scenarios Our findings indicate that the modified LRTs provide substantial improvements in both type I error rates and power establishing them as reliable tools for practitioners facing the challenge of testing covariance matrix homogeneity in multivariate analyses We conclude with applications to realworld datasets that illustrate the practical relevance of our methods

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In the context of environmental monitoring and climate change detecting shifts in vegetation patterns is vital for understanding ecosystem dynamics and informing conservation efforts This paper investigates the application of multiple testing procedures MTPs to identify statistically significant changes in East African vegetation over time Utilizing a comprehensive dataset that spans several decades we employ MTPs such as the Bonferroni correction HolmBonferroni method and false discovery rate FDR controlling procedures to account for the increased risk of Type I errors associated with numerous simultaneous tests Our analysis includes diverse ecological variables derived from satellite imagery and ground observations allowing for an exhaustive assessment of vegetation dynamics across different regions in East Africa We demonstrate how these procedures enhance detection power while maintaining rigorous control over false positives The findings reveal distinct patterns of vegetation change linked to anthropogenic influences and climatic variations highlighting areas of ecological concern and resilience This study underscores the importance of robust statistical frameworks in ecological research and offers insights into the applicability of MTPs in environmental data analysis We conclude that systematic application of MTPs can significantly improve the reliability of change detection in complex ecological datasets ultimately contributing to more informed environmental management strategies in the face of ongoing global change

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In the realm of highdimensional data analysis multiple testing poses significant challenges particularly concerning the risks associated with Type II errors false negatives This paper presents a comprehensive framework for assessing and mitigating the severity of Type II errors in highdimensional multiple testing scenarios We first establish a theoretical foundation highlighting the conditions under which these errors become particularly pronounced complicating the identification of significant effects Our methodology combines advanced statistical techniques including adaptive thresholding and empirical Bayes approaches to refine detection power while controlling the false discovery rate Through a series of simulations and realworld applications we demonstrate our framework s effectiveness in different settings including genomics and neuroimaging where traditional methods often fail to account for the intricate dependence structures present in highdimensional data Our findings underscore the importance of addressing Type II errors in the context of multiple testing providing robust solutions that enhance both statistical inference and practical decisionmaking in research disciplines reliant on highdimensional analytics We conclude with recommendations for best practices in multiple testing procedures and discuss future directions for further research in this critical area

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In the realm of highdimensional hypothesis testing controlling the false discovery rate FDR is a critical concern particularly in the presence of dependent test statistics This paper introduces novel procedures for controlling the KFDR ktrue discoveries false discovery rate using bivariate distributions of null pvalues We begin by establishing a theoretical framework that employs the joint distribution of correlated pvalues allowing for a more accurate estimation of rates of true and false discoveries Our proposed methodologies involve a series of adjustments and thresholds derived from empirical bivariate pvalue distributions which help maintain the KFDR at a specified level while accommodating the inherent dependencies among tests Through extensive simulation studies we demonstrate that our approaches outperform existing methods in various dependency structures including positive and negative correlations We also provide an application of our procedures to real genomic data showcasing their practical utility in identifying significant associations without inflating the risk of erroneous conclusions Overall our findings underscore the importance of incorporating the correlation structure of pvalues to enhance the reliability of statistical inference in highdimensional settings

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: Results on the false discovery rate FDR and the false nondiscovery rate FNR are developed for singlestep multiple testing procedures In addition to verifying desirable properties of FDR and FNR as measures of error rates these results extend previously known results providing further insights particularly under dependence into the notions of FDR and FNR and related measures First considering fixed configurations of true and false null hypotheses inequalities are obtained to explain how an FDR or FNRcontrolling singlestep procedure such as a Bonferroni or Sidak procedure can potentially be improved Two families of procedures are then constructed one that modifies the FDRcontrolling and the other that modifies the FNRcontrolling Sidak procedure These are proved to control FDR or FNR under independence less conservatively than the corresponding families that modify the FDR or FNRcontrolling Bonferroni procedure Results of numerical investigations of the performance of the modified Sidak FDR procedure over its competitors are presented Second considering a mixture model where different configurations of true and false null hypotheses are assumed to have certain probabilities results are also derived that extend some of Storeys work to the dependence case

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: The monotonicity of the critical values is essential for the implementation of a stepup multiple test procedure For a stepup test controlling the family wise error rate exactly at a while a theoretical justification of the existence of monotone critical values is available in the literature for the case of iid test statistics it is still an open problem for the general exchangeable case Recently Finner and Roters Ann Statist gave an example of three exchangeable random variables casting doubt about this existence in general We provide a positive result in this paper by proving that the critical values of a stepup test involving an equicorrelated trivariate standard normal distribution is indeed monotone when the common correlation is positive and at most zalpha zzalpha z where zalpha is the upper alpha percent point of N Our example raises the hope of establishing the desired monotonicity property in the case of test statistics with totally positive multivariate distributions in the sense of Karlin and Rinott C Elsevier Science BV

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: The idea of modifying and potentially improving classical multiple testing methods controlling the familywise error rate FINER via an estimate of the unknown number of true null hypotheses has been around for a long time without a formal answer to the question whether or not such adaptive methods ultimately maintain the strong control of FWER until Finner and Gontscharuk and Guo have offered some answers A class of adaptive Bonferroni and Sidak methods larger than considered in those papers is introduced with the FWER control now proved under a weaker distributional setup Numerical results show that there are versions of adaptive Bonferroni and Sidak methods that can perform better under certain positive dependence situations than those previously considered A different adaptive Holm method and its stepup analog referred to as an adaptive Hochberg method are also introduced and their FWER control is proved asymptotically as in those papers These adaptive Holm and Hochberg methods are numerically seen to often outperform the previously considered adaptive Holm method C Elsevier BV

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: The concept of kFWER has received much attention lately as an appropriate error rate for multiple testing when one seeks to control at least k false rejections for some fixed k A less conservative notion the kFDR has been introduced very recently by Sarkar generalizing the false discovery rate of Benjamini and Hochberg In this article we bring newer insight to the kFDR considering a mixture model involving independent pvalues before motivating the developments of some new procedures that control it We prove the kFDR control of the proposed methods under a slightly weaker condition than in the mixture model We provide numerical evidence of the proposed methods superior power performance over some kFWER and kFDR methods Finally we apply our methods to a real data set

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: The Simes method for testing intersection of more than two hypotheses is known to control the probability of type I error only when the underlying test statistics are independent Although this method is more powerful than the classical Bonferroni method it is not known whether it is conservative when the test statistics are dependent This article proves that for multivariate distributions exhibiting a type of positive dependence that arise in many multiplehypothesis testing situations the Simes method indeed controls the probability of type I error This extends some results established very recently in the special case of two hypotheses

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: Testing multiple null hypotheses in two stages to decide which of these can be rejected or accepted at the first stage and which should be followed up for further testing having had additional observations is of importance in many scientific studies We develop two procedures each with two different combination functions Fishers and Simes to combine pvalues from two stages given prespecified boundaries on the firststage pvalues in terms of the false discovery rate FDR and controlling the overall FDR at a desired level The FDR control is proved when the pairs of firstand secondstage pvalues are independent and those corresponding to the null hypotheses are identically distributed as a pair p p satisfying the pclud property We did simulations to show that our twostage procedures can have significant power improvements over the firststage BenjaminiHochberg BH procedure compared to the improvement offered by the ideal BH procedure that one would have used had the second stage data been available for all the hypotheses and can continue to control the FDR under some dependence situations and can offer considerable cost savings compared to the ideal BH procedure The procedures are illustrated through a real gene expression data Supplementary materials for this article are available online

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: The rising complexity of highdimensional data analysis necessitates robust statistical methods for controlling error rates in hypothesis testing This paper introduces a generalized framework for the False Discovery Rate FDR expanding upon traditional FDR approaches to address diverse data structures and dependencies We propose a novel methodology that incorporates flexible modeling techniques to account for various types of null hypotheses while also integrating prior information and assumptions about the underlying data distribution Our approach enables the estimation of FDR in scenarios with correlated tests hierarchical structures and multistage procedures Theoretical properties including consistency and asymptotic behavior of the proposed estimator are established Extensive simulation studies demonstrate the superior performance of our generalized FDR method relative to existing strategies particularly in challenging settings common in genomics and machine learning applications Lastly we apply our framework to realworld datasets illustrating its practical utility and potential to enhance decisionmaking in largescale testing problems This work not only broadens the theoretical understanding of FDR control but also provides a practical tool for researchers navigating the intricacies of modern statistical analysis

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: Microarray gene expression studies over ordered categories are routinely conducted to gain insights into biological functions of genes and the underlying biological processes Some common experiments are timecoursedoseresponse experiments where a tissue or cell line is exposed to different doses andor durations of time to a chemical A goal of such studies is to identify gene expression author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In repeated measures bioavailabilitybioequivalence studies involving two formulations the underlying measurements such as the area under the plasma concentrationtime curve AUC and the maximum plasma concentration Cmax typically have a block compoundsymmetric covariance matrix To test the equality of the variances in such a covariance matrix we derive in this paper an exact test and four asymptotic tests We compare these tests using simulation to determine those that have good performance in terms of controlling the type I error rate as well as providing good power We provide an example to demonstrate the proposed method Copyright C John Wiley Sons Ltd

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In the realm of multiple hypothesis testing controlling the familywise error rate FWER is crucial for maintaining the reliability of scientific conclusions The Simes method a wellestablished procedure has been traditionally applied under the assumption of independence among test statistics However many practical scenarios involve positively dependent test statistics which can lead to suboptimal performance of standard multiple testing procedures In this paper we extend the Simes method to accommodate positively dependent test statistics by leveraging the concepts of dependence structure and correlation inequalities We conduct a thorough theoretical analysis to establish the validity and efficacy of the modified Simes procedure demonstrating that it maintains control over the FWER while improving power in settings characterized by positive dependence Through a series of Monte Carlo simulations and real data applications we illustrate the advantages of our approach compared to traditional methods Our findings highlight the importance of appropriately accounting for dependency structures in multiple hypothesis testing frameworks and provide a robust alternative for researchers dealing with positively dependent data The proposed methodology is straightforward to implement and contributes to the growing recognition of the complexities involved in modern statistical inference

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In the landscape of multiple hypothesis testing the management of false discoveries and nondiscoveries is crucial for maintaining the integrity of statistical inference This paper systematically investigates the interplay between False Discovery Rates FDR and False Nondiscovery Rates FNR within singlestep multiple testing procedures We introduce a framework that unifies these two concepts allowing for a nuanced understanding of how singlestep procedures can impact both type I and type II errors By conducting extensive simulations and theoretical derivations we characterize the tradeoffs between FDR and FNR under various testing paradigms including the BenjaminiHochberg procedure and its derivatives We reveal that minimizing FDR can inadvertently inflate FNR especially in settings with sparse signals or highdimensional data Our findings highlight the necessity of balancing discovery rates for effective hypothesis testing and we propose practical guidelines for researchers to optimize their procedures The implications of our results extend to fields such as genomics psychology and economics where accurate decisionmaking from multiple tests is imperative This work opens avenues for future research on multifaceted control of error rates in statistical methodologies

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In statistical inference the construction of confidence intervals is pivotal for reliable estimation of population parameters This paper addresses the challenge of deriving shorter confidence intervals for the generalized variance a crucial metric for multivariate data analysis We propose a novel methodology that leverages advanced statistical techniques to enhance the precision and accuracy of confidence intervals associated with the generalized variance By employing a combination of the likelihoodbased approach and bootstrap resampling methods we formulate a new confidence interval that significantly reduces the interval length while maintaining the desired coverage probability Through extensive simulation studies we demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed method compared to existing techniques highlighting improvements in both bias and length of the confidence intervals Additionally we provide a theoretical underpinning for our approach ensuring robustness across various distributions and sample sizes Our findings contribute to the field of multivariate statistics by offering a practical tool for researchers and practitioners seeking more efficient inference methods for generalized variance estimation

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In clinical trials and biomedical research the challenge of controlling false discovery rate FDR while addressing multiple hypotheses is paramount This paper introduces a novel twostage adaptive design framework for multiple testing that incorporates combination tests and accounts for FDR control We develop a comprehensive statistical methodology that first conducts preliminary analyses in the first stage allowing for the adaptation of the testing strategy based on observed outcomes In the second stage we propose combination tests that leverage disparate sources of information to enhance power without compromising FDR control Theoretical properties of the proposed tests are derived establishing their asymptotic behavior and robustness Simulations are conducted to evaluate the performance of our approach in various settings revealing that our method achieves competitive power compared to existing techniques while maintaining stringent control of the FDR We illustrate the practical application of our framework through a case study in genomics demonstrating its utility in identifying significant biomarkers in highdimensional data Our findings highlight the advantage of adaptive designs in multiple testing scenarios paving the way for more efficient and reliable hypothesis testing in research with complex data structures

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: AbstractIn the realm of statistical inference controlling false discoveries is crucial particularly within multidimensional datasets where directional decisions are pivotal This paper addresses the challenges of managing false discovery rates FDR in the context of gene expression data organized into ordered categories We propose a novel framework that adapts existing FDR control methodologies to accommodate the complexities of directional decisions influenced by multiple dimensions Our approach leverages a structured hypothesis testing framework that incorporates the inherent ordering of categories and employs multivariate techniques to enhance power while maintaining rigorous FDR control Through extensive simulations we demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in accurately identifying significant gene expressions while minimizing false discoveries outperforming traditional unidimensional approaches We apply our framework to realworld gene expression data from various biological studies revealing insights into differential expression across ordered categories relevant to disease classification and prognosis Our findings establish a robust methodology for statisticians and biologists alike bridging the gap between directional decisionmaking and rigorous statistical control in highdimensional biological data analysis

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: AbstractIn the realm of multiple hypothesis testing controlling the Familywise Error Rate FWER is a critical concern particularly in studies involving a large number of simultaneous tests This paper introduces novel adaptive procedures designed to enhance the control of the FWER while maintaining high power across a variety of conditions We first explore current methods used in FWER control such as Bonferroni and Holms sequential testing approach identifying their limitations under dependent structures and varying effect sizes Our proposed adaptive procedures leverage datadriven techniques to dynamically adjust significance thresholds based on the observed distribution of pvalues Through extensive simulation studies we demonstrate that our methods effectively reduce the FWER while outperforming traditional approaches in terms of statistical power especially in scenarios characterized by sparsity or highdimensional data We also provide a theoretical framework supporting our adaptive strategies presenting results that guarantee FWER control under specific conditions Our findings contribute to the ongoing discourse in statistical methodology offering researchers improved tools for valid inference in complex experiments and observational studies Finally we discuss practical implications and potential applications of our procedures in diverse fields including genomics psychology and social sciences

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: A multivariate extension of Cohens J Amer Statist Assoc result on interval estimation of normal variance is made in this article Based on independent random matrices X p m and S p p distributed respectively as Npm Im and Wpn with unknown and n p the problem of obtaining confidence interval for is considered The shortest length invariant confidence interval is obtained and is shown to be improved by some other interval estimators Some new properties of the noncentral and central distributions of sample generalized variance have been proved for this purpose

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: This paper explores the relationship between the multivariatet distribution and the Simes inequality a critical tool in multihypothesis testing We begin by providing a comprehensive review of the properties of the multivariatet distribution highlighting its relevance in modeling correlated data particularly in small sample sizes and scenarios with heavytailed distributions We then introduce the Simes inequality and its role in managing Type I error rates in multiple comparison procedures Our analysis presents conditions under which the Simes inequality can be applied to test hypotheses derived from multivariatet distributed variables Through a series of simulations we demonstrate the effectiveness of the Simes inequality in controlling familywise error rates when applied to multivariatet data Furthermore we provide theoretical proofs to establish the robustness of the Simes inequality in this context The findings of this paper contribute to the literature by extending the application of the Simes inequality offering a valuable approach for researchers dealing with multivariate data in various fields including finance biology and social sciences

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: In this paper we investigate the monotonicity properties of critical values associated with a stepup multiple testing procedure Stepup tests are widely employed in the context of controlling the false discovery rate in multiple hypothesis testing and understanding the behavior of critical values in relation to the underlying pvalues is crucial for their effective application We analyze the relationship between the ranking of pvalues and the corresponding critical values generated by a stepup procedure Using theoretical derivations and simulations we demonstrate that under certain regularity conditions the critical values exhibit a monotonic relationship as a function of the ordered pvalues This monotonicity not only provides insights into the structure of the stepup test but also aids in the development of robust methodologies for hypothesis testing Our findings have implications for practitioners in statistical analysis ensuring that the application of stepup tests adheres to stringent criteria for interpretability and reliability Ultimately this note contributes to the understanding of stepup testing frameworks and emphasizes the necessity for further exploration of their theoretical underpinnings

author: Sanat K. Sarkar
text: This study investigates the treatment variances observed in repeated measures bioavailability trials which are crucial for evaluating the efficacy and safety of pharmaceutical formulations Utilizing a diverse dataset comprised of multiple bioavailability studies we applied a mixedeffects model to assess the variability associated with different treatment groups over time Our analysis emphasizes the role of intra and intersubject variability as well as the influence of baseline characteristics on treatment outcomes We employed advanced statistical techniques including ANOVA and nested variance components analysis to compare the treatment variances providing a comprehensive understanding of the sources of variability Our findings reveal significant differences in treatment variances among various formulations highlighting the importance of considering these variances when designing bioavailability studies and interpreting their results These insights pave the way for improved methodologies in drug efficacy assessment and inform regulatory decisionmaking processes in the pharmaceutical industry The results underscore the necessity of careful consideration of treatment variance in the development and approval of new therapeutics
